source_fields.instance: Before interaction, the environment fixes time-dependent reward distributions nu_{t,i} supported on [0,1], with means mu_{t,i}. Rewards are sampled independently across rounds. A public total mean-variation budget V satisfies sum_{t=2}^T ||mu_t-mu_{t-1}||_infinity <= V.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: Every $\nu_{t,i}$ is supported on $[0,1]$. Under the declared model of fresh rewards independent across rounds, the selected arm's observation has its specified current distribution.

assumptions.scope: The objects, time horizon, and variable blocks explicitly declared here; none is inherited from another specification.
assumptions.description: The sum $\sum_{t=2}^T\|\mu_t-\mu_{t-1}\|_\infty$ has a public upper bound. It excludes the initial mean and is not sample-path variation.

source_fields.parameter_domain_description: $K$: $K\in\mathbb N,\ K\ge2$ (public); $T$: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); $V$: $0\le V\le T-1$ (public).
interaction_timing: The environment fixes all $\nu_{t,i}$; $K,T,V$ are public.
The learner chooses $a_t$ from previous samples.
The target is the cumulative gap between the current largest mean and the selected mean.
source_fields.adversary_information: Distributions or functions are fixed before interaction. A round’s fresh sample is drawn after the action and probes are chosen, independently of past history and the learner’s private randomness.
unresolved_applicability: The classical upper and lower theorems match only within the stated V, K, and T window. The T^(2/3) rate is not extrapolated to every variation endpoint.

operations.query_signature: Inputs: $t,\ a_t\in[K]$. Timing and visible information follow the specified protocol.
operations.order_convention: order is relative to the current member f_t(x), f(x), or sample F(x;ξ_t) of the named indexed function family and only with respect to x; finite feedback interfaces have no derivative order

feedback_quality.description: Only one [0,1]-valued sample from the currently selected arm is observed. The same arm's distribution may change next round and is not a fixed nu_i. The mean schedule is fixed in advance; the specification does not include learner-history-dependent environments.

operations.coupling: Only one [0,1]-valued sample from the currently selected arm is observed. The same arm's distribution may change next round and is not a fixed nu_i. The mean schedule is fixed in advance; the specification does not include learner-history-dependent environments.
operations.index_control: The learner selects feasible actions and explicitly permitted probes. The environment controls the current loss, outcome, or fresh sample; the learner cannot select future rounds.
operations.access_schedule: Follow the interaction order in registry.protocols exactly. Current loss feedback follows the action; any pre-action context or advice phase is specified separately.

public_inputs: The public total mean-variation bound V.
auxiliary_interfaces: No additional access to hidden losses, means, or gradients is available. Projection, sampling, and internal optimization over public domains may have separately recorded computation costs; they are not free loss oracles.

source_fields.feasibility: Every loss-bearing action must belong to the action domain. The final output retains the complete action trajectory.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Any measurable computation on received feedback is allowed. No native observation may be added after the budget is exhausted or the algorithm stops.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: Only the stated statistical guarantee is required, not a certificate verifiable through the feedback interface.

source_fields.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: The compared mean losses or rewards lie in $[0,1]$, so cumulative pseudo-regret lies in $[0,T]$.

components.description: Sequential online rounds; only information permitted by the protocol is visible in each round.
A fixed number $T$ of arm pulls, with one reward sample per round.

source_fields.budget_semantics: There are T sequential interaction rounds. Native feedback count is determined by the per-round protocol and is not an independent budget to minimize.
source_fields.scalarization: At fixed T, compare the native cumulative quantity in the objective. Retain the full resource vector; internal optimization, projection, and sampling are not implicitly one loss query.
source_fields.setup_cost: Only declared public inputs may be read. Hidden losses, means, or samples cannot be accessed in advance or outside the $T$ rounds or $\tau$ samples.
source_fields.online_cost: The base bandit strategy may restart using public V, with no extra reward queries from restarting itself. Epoch length, arm-weight maintenance, and sampling are internal computation. Adaptation to unknown V requires a separate information specification.
source_fields.amortization_scope: The algorithm runs on one environment. Charged feedback cannot be reused across independent instances.
source_fields.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.randomization: Private randomization is allowed. The seed is hidden from the environment and independent of the fixed instance and sample randomness.
source_fields.adaptivity: The action and every probe in a round may depend only on previous-round feedback, public inputs, any context or advice already revealed that round, and private randomness. They may not use unrevealed current losses or samples.
restrictions: All measurable causal policies satisfying the declared information timing and feasible domain are allowed, without extra span, iteration-form, or polynomial-time restrictions.
source_fields.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable exact-real computation is permitted; feedback complexity does not imply arithmetic or bit complexity. A base bandit policy may restart using public $V$, without additional reward queries. Restart lengths, arm weights, and sampling are internal computations. Adapting to unknown $V$ requires a different public-information contract.
source_fields.parallelism: Online rounds proceed sequentially. A two-point evaluation is a same-round feedback pair, not two independent rounds.

source_fields.complete_expression: The native target is $\inf_{\mathcal A(K,T,V)}\sup_{(\nu_{t,i}):\ \mathrm{VarPath}(\mu)\le V}\mathbb E_{\mathcal A,\nu}[R_T]$.
aggregation_order: Take the infimum over algorithms knowing only public K, T, and supplied budgets.
Take the supremum over admissible time-varying distribution schedules fixed before interaction.
The comparator is the deterministic largest mean $\mu_t^\star$ in each round, without switching costs.
Expectation covers learner randomness and the selected reward samples. The objective is cumulative mean gap, not comparison with the best realized reward trajectory in hindsight.
source_fields.quantifier_order: One learning algorithm must apply to every instance in the declared class. It may use public inputs only, not hidden instance parameters.
source_fields.time_uniformity: The T-round horizon is fixed and public. No anytime or simultaneous-all-T high-probability guarantee is implied.

source_fields.budget_semantics: There are T sequential interaction rounds. Native feedback count is determined by the per-round protocol and is not an independent budget to minimize.
source_fields.precision_model: Observations and internal arithmetic use the exact-real model. No bit-complexity claim follows.
source_fields.scalarization: At fixed T, compare the native cumulative quantity in the objective. Retain the full resource vector; internal optimization, projection, and sampling are not implicitly one loss query.

description_paragraphs: Arm reward distributions may change over time, but total mean variation has a known upper bound. The learner samples one arm per round and competes with that round's best mean arm. The variation budget constrains the environment and is not a comparator-path-length bound.

description_paragraphs: Reward distributions $\nu_{t,i}$ depend on time and are fixed before interaction. They are supported on $[0,1]$ and need not be identically distributed over time.
For the arm means $\mu_t$, total variation sums infinity-norm differences of successive mean vectors from $t=2$. The initial mean vector is not charged.
The public total mean-variation budget $V$ is neither the variation of a realized observation path nor the number of best-arm switches.
Require $K\ge2$, $T\ge1$, and $0\le V\le T-1$, with actions in $[K]$.
The classical matching region has additional restrictions. The endpoint V = 0 and other boundaries have separate coverage records.
